newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut banks in secondary Lebanese CDs trade.
newsitem.headline: Beirut banks in secondary Lebanese CDs trade.

text.p: Two Beirut banks have carried out the first secondary market trade in Lebanese government certificates of deposit, officials at the banks said on Tuesday.
Citibank Beirut sold Banque Audi central bank CDs worth two billion Lebanese pounds in a trial trade on Monday, they said.
"We did a small amount to test the system to see if it is do-able," a Citibank Beirut official told Reuters by telephone.
"We hope other banks will start trading in the secondary market," he added. "We would strongly welcome other participants."
The Bank of Lebanon introduced the 45- and 60-day CDs two years ago but no secondary market trade has developed until now.
The officials at the two banks cited the central bank's recent reduction in allotments of Lebanese treasury bills as a primary reason for seeking to develop a secondary market in CDs.

"We saw that the secondary market in securities was drying up a bit because of the partial allotments, so in lieu of this we decided to develop secondary market trading in CDs as a way to provide short-term liquidity," the Citibank official said.
Subscriptions to the Bank of Lebanon's weekly CD issues, which are open only to banks, have jumped since t-bill allotments were restricted.
Last week's CD issue was 93 billion Lebanese pounds. Previous issues were sometimes three billion pounds or less as investors concentrated on t-bills.

"Because of structural reasons the CDs were being bought and held to maturity," the Banque Audi official said. One reason for this was the divisibility of the certificates, but this matter had been settled in discussions by Citibank officials with the central bank, he added.
